title: GDP in current US dollars
summary: India’s GDP measured in current US dollars rose in the World Bank series; it remained below $5 trillion in 2025.
method: Calendar-year nominal GDP in USD (WDI NY.GDP.MKTP.CD). Exchange-rate movements affect comparisons; not a measure of real income or living standards.
confidence: High for the reported WDI series

title: Real GDP growth, revised base
summary: Real GDP continued to grow strongly in the new 2022–23-base series.
method: Latest September 2026 MoSPI updates; FY24–25 First Revised Estimate, FY25–26 Provisional Estimate. Do not append old-base pre-2022 growth figures as if they formed the same series.
confidence: High within the 2022–23-base series

title: Headline CPI inflation
summary: Headline inflation increased between July and August 2026 under the 2024 CPI base.
method: Jul 2026 final and Aug 2026 provisional (year-on-year rate). These are two observations, not a long-run cost-of-living series. CPI rebased to 2024=100.
confidence: High for release; August provisional

title: Consumer food inflation
summary: Food inflation was higher than headline CPI inflation in August 2026.
method: Consumer Food Price Index, combined rural and urban, 2024 base; August observation provisional.
confidence: High for release; August provisional

title: CPI inflation by location · Aug 2026
summary: Rural headline inflation was higher than urban inflation in August 2026.
method: Cross-section for ONE MONTH, not a time trend. Rural 5.23%, urban 4.31%, August provisional.
confidence: High for release; provisional

title: Rural consumption per person
summary: Reported real monthly consumption per rural resident is higher in the latest survey than in 2011–12.
method: HCES average MPCE at 2011–12 prices, excluding imputed free welfare items. 2011–12 and 2022–24 surveys differ in design and reference period; headline comparison is indicative, not seamless. Consumption is not salary.
confidence: Official data; historical comparability qualified

title: Urban consumption per person
summary: Reported inflation-adjusted monthly consumption per urban resident rose in the surveyed periods.
method: HCES monthly MPCE at 2011–12 prices, excluding welfare imputation; survey-method changes limit direct long-run comparisons. Not a measure of disposable income.
confidence: Official data; historical comparability qualified

title: Union fiscal deficit · budget comparisons
summary: The budget estimates a slightly lower fiscal deficit for FY2026–27 than its FY2025–26 revised estimate.
method: RE is revised estimate; BE is budget estimate, NOT final actual. Only Union finances; never label the forecast a delivered result.
confidence: High as published budget estimates

title: Union government debt · budget comparisons
summary: The budget projects a reduction in the Union debt-to-GDP ratio.
method: Centre only, not consolidated state and Union public debt. Both points are budget estimates, not realised observations. Target 50±1% by 2030–31.
confidence: High as published budget estimates

title: Poverty at $4.20/day (2021 PPP)
summary: The World Bank estimates a substantial decline in poverty at its lower-middle-income line.
method: World Bank Oct 2025 India Poverty & Equity Brief; $4.20/person/day in 2021 PPP. WB harmonises the survey inputs; figures span both pre- and post-2014 years. Not solely attributable to one government.
confidence: High as World Bank estimates; model and survey caveats

title: Extreme poverty at $3/day (2021 PPP)
summary: The World Bank Oct 2025 brief reports a decline in extreme poverty under its $3/day line.
method: 2021 PPP, $3.00/person/day; do not mix with older $2.15 (2017 PPP) figures (e.g. 16.2% to 2.3%). Revision vintage and survey adjustments matter.
confidence: High as World Bank estimates; model and survey caveats

title: Consumption-based inequality (Gini)
summary: Consumption Gini declined in the World Bank’s harmonised survey estimates.
method: Consumption-based Gini, not income or wealth Gini; top incomes may be undercounted, and income inequality can move differently.
confidence: Qualified by survey and construct limits

title: Manufacturing share of GVA
summary: Manufacturing’s share of total GVA remained around 15% in these revised estimates.
method: Current-price manufacturing GVA divided by total GVA; new 2022–23 base. FY24–25 First Revised Estimate; FY25–26 Provisional Estimate. Does not measure manufacturing employment or real output growth.
confidence: High within revised accounts

title: Total gross FDI inflows
summary: Gross FDI inflows increased between FY2013–14 and FY2024–25.
method: Gross FDI inflows, not net FDI or new greenfield investment. Last figure provisional; does not by itself establish jobs created or investment productivity.
confidence: High as official gross-inflow figures

title: Real GDP growth · World Bank annual series
summary: Yearly growth varies substantially, including the pandemic contraction and subsequent rebound. Pre/post decade averages describe periods, not causal effects.
method: World Bank WDI NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG, calendar-year release 8 Oct 2026. This series is not numerically interchangeable with MoSPI FY 2022–23-base real GDP revisions; no cross-vintage splicing.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Annual consumer inflation · World Bank/IMF
summary: Annual inflation was substantially higher during several pre-2014 years, but later years also experienced price pressure. An inflation rate is not a price level.
method: World Bank WDI FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (source IMF IFS), calendar-year percent changes 2004–2025, lastupdated 2026-10-08. Distinct from India's monthly 2026 CPI=2024-base releases.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Illustrative cumulative price index (2004=100)
summary: Prices can keep rising even when the inflation rate falls; this index illustrates compounding of annual CPI changes.
method: Derived: index_2004=100; index_t=index_(t−1)×(1+annual WDI CPI inflation_t/100), using 2005–2025 annual rates. This is a synthetic chain index, not an official CPI level or household-specific basket.
confidence: Derived from WDI published values; household relevance varies

title: Union gross fiscal deficit · historical
summary: The central fiscal deficit fell in the mid-2010s but rose sharply during COVID-19; later estimates show consolidation.
method: RBI Annual Report 2023–24 Key Fiscal Indicators table; FY 2023–24 revised estimate and FY 2022–23 estimate in publication. Percent GDP, Centre only (not consolidated state+Centre).
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Union outstanding liabilities · historical
summary: Centre outstanding liabilities changed over time, with an increase during the pandemic and later estimated decline.
method: RBI Key Fiscal Indicators, Outstanding Liabilities ($) column for Centre; must not be equated with general-government (centre + states) debt. FY2023–24 is a revised estimate.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Net household financial savings
summary: Household net financial savings fluctuated substantially; these are national-accounts aggregates, not median household disposable savings.
method: RBI Annual Report 2022–23 Table II.2.2, same historic vintage 2011–12 to 2021–22. Later RBI publications revised some estimates and use additional sources; do not attach those without revisions.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Household financial liabilities flow
summary: Household new financial liabilities rose and fell across this period; the series measures a flow, not household debt stock.
method: RBI Annual Report 2022–23 Table II.2.2, Financial Liabilities row, % GNDI. This is not household debt as a percentage of GDP.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Extreme poverty · 2026 World Bank revision
summary: World Bank staff estimates show a large decline, while warning that the underlying survey instruments and harmonisation methodology changed.
method: World Bank India Development Update April 2026 figure 2.6. Using 2021 PPP $3.00 line; do not mix with legacy $2.15 (2017 PPP) or with 2022–23 figures from a different update vintage.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Rural extreme poverty · World Bank
summary: Revised poverty estimate shows lower rural poverty, but comparability depends on World Bank survey adjustments.
method: World Bank April 2026 India Development Update Figure 2.6; 2021 PPP; harmonised welfare measures.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Urban extreme poverty · World Bank
summary: Urban poverty declined in the estimated survey series; the measure says nothing alone about income inequality or quality of jobs.
method: World Bank April 2026 India Development Update Figure 2.6; 2021 PPP, harmonised HCES based data.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Moderate poverty · updated World Bank
summary: Updated World Bank estimates show lower measured poverty at the lower-middle-income international line.
method: World Bank India Development Update 2026 Figure 2.7; 2021 PPP $4.20 LMIC line, survey harmonisation. Use a single 2026 data vintage for both endpoints.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Top 1% wealth share · independent estimate
summary: Research estimates substantial wealth concentration; this is not directly comparable to consumption poverty or Gini.
method: World Inequality Lab authors; published in World Bank Economic Review May 2026; estimates combine wealth, survey, tax and rich-list evidence. 2022–23 point only; not a verified 2014→2026 series.
confidence: Model-based independent estimate; uncertainty and data-quality limitations

title: Top 1% income share · independent estimate
summary: A published 2026 revision estimates income concentration at 23.3% for 2022–23; earlier working-paper vintage reported 22.6%.
method: May 2026 World Bank Economic Review peer-reviewed version; replaces earlier preliminary working paper’s 22.6% estimate. Not the same variable as consumption distribution.
confidence: Model-based peer-reviewed estimate; data-quality limitations

title: Gross investment · IMF definition
summary: Investment remained above 30% of GDP in the cited IMF estimates; this is not identical to private-sector investment.
method: IMF 2025 Article IV published 2025, selected social and economic indicators; 2024–25 estimate may be revised in later publications. Not a direct manufacturing-output metric.
confidence: IMF published macroeconomic table; vintage Nov 2025

title: Gross national savings · IMF aggregate
summary: Overall gross savings are distinct from household net financial savings; national aggregate does not reveal household distribution.
method: IMF 2025 Article IV Table 1. Aggregated saving (not the household financial net-savings series).
confidence: IMF macroeconomic table, release vintage 2025

title: General-government deficit · IMF
summary: Central plus state deficit differs from Union-only fiscal deficit; the distinction is essential.
method: IMF 2025 Article IV published fiscal table, general-government balance rendered as absolute deficits. Includes state governments and differs in scope from RBI central deficit.
confidence: IMF 2025 Article IV; estimate and revision caveats

title: Merchandise exports · annual USD values
summary: Merchandise exports in current US dollars increased since FY2013–14, but changed little between FY2023–24 and FY2024–25.
method: Ministry of Commerce 2025 releases. The FY2013–14 figure is a rounded figure from a retrospective release, so long-run percentage changes should be labelled approximate. Goods, not services; current US dollars, not constant price volumes.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Merchandise trade deficit · latest FYs
summary: The merchandise deficit widened across these two fiscal years; a larger trade deficit cannot alone determine wider national economic performance.
method: Ministry of Commerce 2024–25 merchandise exports and imports, merchandise trade deficit magnitude. Excludes net services trade. No comparable pre-2014 values in this curated extract.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Urban / rural real consumption ratio
summary: Urban monthly real consumption per person remained higher than rural consumption in both surveys.
method: Derived from the separately sourced real MPCE 2011–12-price observations in the existing economic research register; the ratio is indicative given HCES methodology revisions.
confidence: Survey harmonisation limitations

title: Real GDP per capita · PPP adjusted
summary: Real output per person increased over the period, but average GDP per capita is not median household income.
method: UNdata World Bank WDI NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD, source vintage Feb 2026; calendar year 2004–2024. Do not splice with MoSPI FY series of another base year.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: General government gross debt · IMF
summary: IMF debt measurement includes central and state governments; it is not the Union-only public debt measure.
method: IMF 2025 Article IV Table 1. General-government debt, FY and vintage as published.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Union gross tax revenue
summary: Tax revenue increased as a share of GDP in some later years. The first point is a multiyear average, not a year.
method: RBI Annual Report Table II.6.1; FY2023–24 is revised estimate and FY2024–25 is budget estimate. Gross tax and net tax revenue differ.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Union capital expenditure
summary: Capital expenditure rose compared with the earlier government fiscal period, but allocations do not certify completed infrastructure.
method: RBI Annual Report fiscal performance Table II.6.1. Mixed historical average, actual, RE and BE labels, not a consistent annual estimate series.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Real manufacturing GVA growth · new base
summary: Revised-base real manufacturing GVA grew in each available year; its share of total GVA remained near 15% in these estimates.
method: MoSPI parliament August 2026; 2022–23-base estimates, FY2024–25 first revised and FY2025–26 provisional. Not directly comparable to earlier 2011–12-base sector series.
confidence: High for documented release; interpretation limited

title: Union interest payments / revenue receipts
summary: Interest payments absorb a substantial portion of central revenue receipts; the latest value is a budget estimate.
method: PRS Union Budget 2024–25 analysis reports 37% of revenue receipts for FY2024–25 Budget Estimate; PRS interim budget comparison cites 37% for FY2013–14. Comparative sources use different budget releases and remain indicative.
confidence: Parliamentary budget analysis, final FY2024–25 estimate not an actual

title: Unemployment rate
summary: Measured unemployment fell in this PLFS series. This does not measure wage adequacy or underemployment; definitions and survey coverage matter.
method: PLFS usual status, persons 15+, nationwide. Measured unemployment fell in this PLFS series. This does not measure wage adequacy or underemployment; definitions and survey coverage matter.
confidence: Source-specific assessment; consult limitations and original publication

title: Female labour-force participation
summary: Participation rose in the PLFS series. Paid work, unpaid household enterprise participation, and quality of employment need separate evaluation.
method: PLFS usual status, women aged 15+. Participation rose in the PLFS series. Paid work, unpaid household enterprise participation, and quality of employment need separate evaluation.

title: Female worker population ratio
summary: A higher worker ratio does not establish adequate earnings or causal attribution to a single government.
method: PLFS usual status, women aged 15+. A higher worker ratio does not establish adequate earnings or causal attribution to a single government.

summary: Freedom House classifies India as Partly Free in its 2025 edition. This is an expert-assessed index, not an objectively measured government performance percentage; editions are labelled, not assumed identical to calendar years.
method: External indices with methodology notes. Freedom House classifies India as Partly Free in its 2025 edition. This is an expert-assessed index, not an objectively measured government performance percentage; editions are labelled, not assumed identical to calendar years.

method: Access Now KeepItOn recorded events. Access Now recorded 116 in 2023 and 84 in 2024. Incident counts are not equivalent to total affected people, geographical area or duration; state and Union authority must be differentiated.
